Step 1: Understand the historical context of the U.S. civil rights movement regarding bus segregation.
Step 2: Recall that while Rosa Parks is the most famous for her 1955 arrest which sparked the Montgomery bus boycott, she was not actually the first person to take this action.
Step 3: Identify Claudette Colvin, a 15-year-old high school student in Montgomery, Alabama, who was arrested on March 2, 1955—nine months before Rosa Parks—for refusing to give up her bus seat to a white passenger.
Step 4: Match this historical fact with the given options. Option (B) correctly identifies Claudette Colvin as the first person.

Final answer: B
